correctness.rationale: Direct inversion of the displayed class-two law gives uv'^T-u'v^T for x^(-1)y^(-1)xy, also in characteristic two. No nonzero vector-coordinate pair is central, and every scalar multiple of a matrix unit occurs as a commutator, so the center equals the derived subgroup. All central inputs are free, giving q^(2kab). With d=2k, concatenate columns u_i,u'_i and rows v_i'^T,-v_i^T to get a bijection between reduced inputs and matrices X,Y through dimension d with XY=C. For C of rank r, choosing a t-dimensional image of X containing im C, then a surjection onto it, then one lift of each column of C gives the reduced count ∑_{t=r}^{min(a,d)} [a-r choose t-r]_q ∏_{i<t}(q^d-q^i) q^{b(d-t)}. For d=2 this expands to all the stated rank-0, rank-1 and rank-2 entries and zero for r>2. Rank subadditivity and pairing a rank-one decomposition verify the least length ceil(r/2), with identity length zero and width at maximal possible rank. Counting rank-r maps by image, kernel and the induced isomorphism from quotient to image gives R_r. For the displayed Fourier version each independent outer product has normalized transform q^(-s) on rank-s dual matrices by orthogonality of a nontrivial additive character. Inversion of d such terms gives the exponent d(a+b-s)-ab. Summing the pairing over maps with image in a subspace S gives q^(a dim S) exactly when C annihilates S, and zero otherwise; Möbius inversion gives the stated Gaussian K_s(r), unchanged by negation. The finite comparison concerns the formulas, not independent field-arithmetic enumeration; the general proof is in RESULT.md steps 1–4 and the lifting count above.

The advertised all-k sum is exactly its evaluation at t=q^(-2k), multiplied by the elementary input and inversion normalization. The proof of this identification is the direct commutator-to-matrix-product encoding and one-character average; it supplies no new rank-transform or word-distribution phenomenon.
